title: Where is the other outcome?
hook: A simulated oracle can show the outcome each person did not receive.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: for each person, only one potential outcome is ever observed; the other column is blank.

misconception: Treating the missing half as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: for each person, only one potential outcome is ever observed; the other column is blank.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Four simulated people have Y₀=[1,4,2,5] and Y₁=[3,5,2,9]. Only one outcome is observed per person. If an oracle reveals both, what is their average treatment effect?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-the-missing-half/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Four people have potential outcomes Y0=[1,4,2,5],Y1=[3,5,2,9]. Assignment[0,1,0,1] reveals[1,5,2,9], hides[3,4,2,5]. Full simulatedATE(2+1+0+4)/4=1.75 only after revealing unavailable oracle values.
